calendar.name: Big Bear — Local Events
calendar.description: A practical, independently curated calendar of worthwhile Big Bear Valley events, with lineups, prices, logistics, source links, conflicts, and honest TBD flags.

events.title: Music in the Mountains — Journey + Bryan Adams Tributes

location.name: Big Bear Discovery Center Amphitheater
location.address: 40971 North Shore Dr, Fawnskin, CA 92333

pricing: $39 general admission to $59 premium, plus any ticket fees shown at checkout
Youth age 12 and under are free
Optional premium on-site parking: $30 per vehicle
events.summary: A polished classic-rock tribute night in the forest: DSB performs Journey, with Summer of ’69 opening with a Bryan Adams tribute. Proceeds support the Southern California Mountains Foundation.
schedule: 4:30–10:00 PM — free shuttle from the Meadows Edge trailhead parking area
5:00 PM — gates, venue parking, food and beverage sales open
6:30–9:30 PM — published music window; exact opener, intermission and headliner times are not posted
9:00 PM — food and beverage sales end
details: General-admission seating is first-come; bring a chair or blanket. The organizer says low-profile chairs are not recommended
Premium seating is unassigned seating provided by the venue
Outside food is allowed. Drinks are limited to sealed water or an empty refillable bottle; refill stations are available
Beer, wine, cocktails, food and nonalcoholic drinks are sold on site
Well-behaved dogs on short leashes are allowed
Bags, coolers, chairs and handbags are subject to search; weapons are prohibited
Rain or shine when conditions are safe; tickets are nonrefundable, and wildfire, weather or another unsafe condition can force cancellation
tips: Free parking is about a quarter-mile west at Meadows Edge; use the organizer’s free shuttle
Six free accessible parking spaces at the Discovery Center are first-come with a state placard or plate; additional accessible premium spaces may be purchased if available
Organizer contact: info@mountainsfoundation.org or 909-382-2790
tbd: Exact set times inside the 6:30–9:30 PM music window have not been published

events.title: Lakefest — New Americana Night

location.name: Ski Beach Park / Swim Beach
location.address: 41216 Park Ave, Big Bear Lake, CA 92315

pricing: Free general admission; the registration page offers a $0 general-admission ticket
Food and drinks are sold separately
events.summary: Lakefest’s Friday opening combines an afternoon farmers market and lakefront festival with stand-up comedy between four New Americana and indie-leaning music sets.
schedule: 3:00 PM — farmers market, beer garden, food vendors, kids zone and yard games open
details: Spencer Someday describes the project as emotionally charged, guitar-driven indie rock built around personal storytelling
The festival also advertises a beer garden, food vendors/trucks, kids activities, yard games, local art and a vendor village
Reliable first-party style descriptions were not found for B!ff or Tristan and Delaney, so their sound is left unclassified
tips: Visit Big Bear says there is no on-site parking; consider the free trolley or bike valet
A satellite lot is advertised near Fox Farm Road and Garstin Drive, but the published shuttle-day wording conflicts with the Friday–Saturday event dates; verify before relying on it
The organizer has not published specific accessibility arrangements; use the registration-page contact form for accommodations
tbd: Satellite parking/shuttle operating days need confirmation because the official tourism page says Saturday and Sunday for a Friday–Saturday festival

location.name: Ski Beach Park / Swim Beach

location.name: Multiple venues: Convention Center, Discovery Center & Snow Summit
location.address: Big Bear Lake, CA 92315

events.summary: Day one of Big Bear’s dark-sky festival: NASA/Caltech science, an immersive AstroDome, a free family DiscoverFest, mountaintop telescopes and night hikes, plus separately ticketed sound-bath and astrophotography experiences.

1:00 PM — Caltech researcher Cameron Hummels: The Science of Black Holes
2:00 PM — NASA scientist Dominic Benford: Expanding Our View with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope

6:30–8:00 PM — separately ticketed Forest Sound Bath at Snow Summit
8:00–11:00 PM — Stargaze at the Summit at Snow Summit, 880 Summit Blvd: Sky Chair, telescopes, guided night hikes, night-sky talks and live painting
8:30–10:30 PM — beginner/intro astrophotography workshop; separately ticketed and sold out when checked
details: SkyFest celebrates astronomy and dark-sky conservation across three venues
A festival pass covers AstroFestival and Stargaze at the Summit, not the sound bath or astrophotography workshop
The 3-day pass was $99 and sold out when checked
tips: Tickets and reservations are activity- and date-specific; check live availability before going
No authoritative event-specific parking or accessibility instructions were found on the current event and ticket pages
tbd: The ticket page describes DiscoverFest as 4:00–9:00 PM and appears to imply all three days; the more detailed official program says Friday/Saturday only, 5:00–8:00 PM. This calendar uses the detailed program
